messages:
Priya Sinha: @channel alert: spike in 5xx for eu canary — IncidentBot paged oncall.
IncidentBot: [ALERT] service-proxy-eu canary error-rate 5m avg > 5% — paging #incidents and oncall.
Kenji Tanaka: I'm taking the page, jumping to call. Can someone own customer comms?
Samir Gupta: I'll do comms. Quick look: 502s concentrated on the blue canary variant.
Ethan Cole: From prod: `curl -i https://canary.eu.redwood.ai/health` returns HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway — envoy.
Kenji Tanaka: DNS lookup: `dig +short canary.eu.redwood.ai` returning mix of IPs: 10.11.12.13 (blue), 10.11.12.14 (green). Some clients hit blue, some green.
Priya Sinha: We swapped blue->green canary ~10m ago; TTL set to 300s but looks like some caches still resolving to blue. Could be stale resolver cache or load-balancer affinity.
DeployBot: Deploy 17690: canary rollout eu-west started at 1769012280, blue->green progressive swap (10% traffic).
Samir Gupta: Impact estimate: ~12% of EU requests saw blue and 502s, others succeeded on green.
SupportBot: Opened customer incident ticket and updated initial status. Next update scheduled in 15m.
Kenji Tanaka: Envoy upstream logs on blue nodes: connection refused / connection reset while proxying to nginx upstream.
Ethan Cole: SSH to 10.11.12.13 (blue): nginx running but access logs show upstream resets: `recv() failed (104: Connection reset by peer) while reading response header from upstream`.
Priya Sinha: Mitigation options: 1) flip routing feature flag to stop sending traffic to blue, 2) force DNS to only resolve to green (risky), 3) immediate rollback of canary. Thoughts?
Kenji Tanaka: We have kill-switch CLI: `ff_control --env eu stop blue_canary_route`. I'll run that. Also pausing the rollout with DeployBot to prevent more movement.
Kenji Tanaka: @DeployBot pause canary now
DeployBot: Canary rollout paused at 1769012390 by kenji.
Kenji Tanaka: Flipped feature flag kill-switch. Verifying: `dig +short canary.eu.redwood.ai` now primarily returns 10.11.12.14 (green).
Ethan Cole: Sampling traffic after flip: 200 requests observed, 0 routed to blue. Error rate back to baseline ~0.4%.
Samir Gupta: Great. Updating customers: mitigation applied by disabling canary routing; engineering investigating root cause on blue pool.
SupportBot: Posted status: "Partial canary routing issue in EU mitigated via routing rollback. Engineers investigating."
Priya Sinha: Action items: collect nginx/core logs from blue nodes, verify recent package/config changes applied to blue-only, and check DNS TTL handling across our CDN and internal resolvers.
Kenji Tanaka: Oncall plan: I'll stay on the incident for 30 more minutes. If unresolved at 1769013000, page Ethan for escalation.
Ethan Cole: Preparing rollback artifact (commit 1a2b3c) in case we need to revert image. Also going to repro by reverting the nginx upgrade on one blue node.
Samir Gupta: Early hypothesis: an nginx package upgrade rolled out to blue pool earlier today and may be dropping keepalive connections after reload. Reproducing on a canary blue node.
Kenji Tanaka: Uploaded logs and traces to /incidents/1769012345/artifacts. Also adding a short runbook describing the kill-switch and the pause we did.
Priya Sinha: Postmortem items: (a) ensure canary routing kill-switch is a one-click Console action, (b) add automated rollbacks when canary error >5% for 5 minutes, (c) audit DNS cache TTL interactions with our CDNs and edge caches.
Samir Gupta: Closing the page for now. Will reopen if we see recurrence. Keeping the thread updated with RCA and remediation timeline. :white_check_mark:
